analysis:
Integration pass over a Flint paged-only change set. Production changes: (1) EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift lines 80-89 stop applying the provider-wide `global` default to Flint. Explicit env or per-model non-native selections still throw flintRequiresNative, and the result stays .native. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift lines ~180-183 promote .auto to .paged for FlintModel, which bypasses the automatic crash-loop guard. Lines ~222-227 throw pagedUnavailable for any non-paged resolution. Both are fail-closed refinements that narrow the contiguous fallback for one model family. (3) ModelBenchmarkNativeQwen4.swift and ThroughputSweep.swift are operator-run benchmark tooling: Flint is routed to the native CBv2 session and its scalar prefill pass is skipped. The rest of the PR is docs, a changelog entry and tests that encode the same fail-closed behavior; the tests set the prefix cache off and use temp roots.

Threat relevance: T-041 and TB-007 are touched only indirectly. Nothing visible changes the SSD tier HMAC lookup tags, 30-minute TTL, cacheSalt scoping, DBK3 crypto, KEK purge or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate. The coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest authorization and key custody are untouched. The residual effect is availability: a Flint load is refused rather than degraded to contiguous when the paged kill switch, a capability veto, the crash-loop guard or a construction failure applies. That is deliberate and affects only the operator's own machine and Flint.

Unverified: the full prepareProductionBackend body between the new override and the refusal check, since the diff shows only partial context. Also unverified are EngineV2SlotFactory and other construction paths, and whether the paged Flint path preserves the SSD cacheSalt and HMAC bindings. These look like correctness questions rather than evidenced regressions, so no findings are raised.
